Subject: Private infra upgrade request — maintenance window and rollback details

Monica,

We'd like to schedule the next minor version rollout for our private Redwood deployment (VPC) — target is the 2027-03-18 week. Before we lock a time, we need confirmation on three things:

1) Version shelving: can you confirm that we can pin our fleet to the current v1.14.2 and opt into a controlled stage for v1.15.0? We can't accept an automatic global bump.
2) Maintenance windows: propose two candidate windows (one overnight M-F, one weekend) and the expected user impact (latency, possible request failures).
3) Rollback criteria and expected RTO: what conditions cause an immediate revert versus a staged mitigation?

Also include any runbooks or preflight checks we should run. We need this to feed our change advisory board on Friday.

Thanks,
Aaron West
Senior Ops Lead
Maple Health Systems

Quick ops plan (high level) — please iterate if I missed anything:

Preflight (T-48h):
- Full infra snapshot and exported KV caches (store to their S3 endpoint).
- Confirm RBAC for canary toggles; ensure customer KMS keys are accessible for the upgrade images.
- Dry-run smoke cycle in staging using a cloned subset (no DB migrations).

Window and sequencing:
- Candidate 1 (preferred): Thu 2027-03-18 01:00-05:00 PT
- Candidate 2 (fallback): Sat 2027-03-20 02:00-06:00 PT
- Staged rollout: 10% canary (30m), 50% (45m), 100% (up to 90m). Pause and observe after each gate.

Network/traffic handling:
- Perform node cordon -> drain KV cache to disk -> start new binaries -> warm KV layer from exported snapshot for canary nodes only.
- Use TCP drain time target: 45s; connection-tolerant draining with graceful shutdown.

Rollback criteria (instant revert iff any of the following):
- Crash-loop observed on >2 canary nodes within 20m
- End-to-end synthetic failure rate >5% compared to baseline for 15m
- Latency P95 regression >200ms sustained across canary set for 10m

Rollback mechanics and RTO:
- Instant shelve to v1.14.2 (we keep last-known-good images cached) — expected RTO 6–12 minutes for canary subset, 20–40 minutes for full fleet depending on drain/warm times.
- If symptoms are partial (config or kernel mismatch), escalate to staged traffic split and targeted rollback per pool.

Post-cutover validation:
- Run smoke tests, sampling-based token-level correctness checks, and runbook checklist (see attached runbook).

Attachments: private-upgrade-runbook.md (contains exact CLI steps, Prometheus queries, and runbook checklist).

Notes on pinning: we will not auto-advance any pinned instances; control-plane will require an explicit canary toggle from Maple's admin role or the approved Redwood contact.

-Karthik
